original_test_intent: Verify the actual configured memory transfer rate reported for every Type 17 device, using the applicable SMBIOS field name, offset, units and any extended representation, and confirm it matches the approved platform configuration and remains correct after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw Type 17 records, SMBIOS version and formatted length; locate configured-speed fields by schema rather than display label, bind them to locator/module identity, apply unknown/extended rules and MT/s normalization, distinguish configured rate from capable Speed, compare approved BIOS/platform policy and repeat after reboot.
manual_activity: A user approves the configured-rate policy and reboot plan. No frequency-setting change is part of this read-only case.
required_inputs: Expected configured transfer rate per device/locator or topology class
Applicable SMBIOS version, structure length, field name/offset and units
Unknown and extended configured-speed selector policy where applicable
Allowed relationship to module capable Speed and platform down-clock limits
Raw-capable parser and approved reboot/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS/BIOS/BMC/OS context; do not change frequency, timings or firmware.
Locate fields by versioned schema/offset and preserve raw values; decoded label is secondary.
Keep configured transfer rate distinct from module capable Speed and physical clock; state units explicitly.
Gate any extended configured-speed field by structure length and selector semantics.
Stop on truncated/mismatched schema, impossible relation or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Parse per-device configured-rate fields by schema, normalize MT/s, validate expected capable/configured relationships and compare pre/post reboot evidence.
Do not alter BIOS settings, stress memory or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve configured-speed baseline, topology/down-clock rules and schema/unit interpretation.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The legacy label identifies the intended field on some tools, but exact grep can miss renamed output and cannot prove field offset/length, locator, units or distinction from capable Speed.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 17 data with SMBIOS version/length; report locator, raw configured/extended fields, selector/unknown decision, normalized MT/s and capable Speed separately.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The configured-speed scope, Type 17 script and 5/5-minute values are retained; log clearing and frequency/BIOS changes are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse the version-appropriate configured-speed offset and extension independent of dmidecode wording, normalize MT/s, compare approved platform topology/down-clock policy and repeat after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 17 devices across revisions that rename or extend configured-speed reporting.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS/BMC, dmidecode/raw-parser and optional SPD-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 17 configured memory speed/clock and extended configured-speed definitions plus authoritative platform memory configuration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces label-dependent grep with version/length/offset-aware raw parsing and capable-versus-configured separation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects renamed-label misses, truncated offsets, wrong units/extended selectors and configuration values attached to the wrong module.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Per-locator configured rate and versioned schema policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware metadata does not independently prove actual electrical clock or stability; performance/signal validation is a separate test.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve lower configured rates for topology, CPU or qualification limits, but must record the rule and preserve capable versus configured values separately; no automatic demand to run at module maximum is implied.
expected_evidence: Approved platform/module identity, per-locator configured-rate and capable/configured policy
Complete pre-reboot raw Type 17 records with SMBIOS version/length
Per-device raw configured/extended fields, schema/selector/unknown result and normalized MT/s
Read-only BIOS/BMC/OS context and capable Speed comparison labeled by source
Approved reboot/health evidence and post-reboot semantic configured-rate diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The legacy item name and newer decoded label refer to the same versioned configured-rate field; schema rather than label resolves the wording.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Schema-aware decoding and configuration comparison are fully automatable after approved inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Replaces fragile legacy-label grep with raw schema, locator, unit and capable/configured analysis.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains label/offset/version safeguards while restoring FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds extended configured-rate handling where applicable and separates metadata from runtime validation/verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a false missing result after a tool label rename and prevents capable Speed from being mistaken for the actual configured rate.
independent_technical_reasoning: Versioned offsets, raw numeric fields and topology policies can be parsed and compared deterministically without changing memory configuration.
